To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the DIS distributions are very close to the MS distributions at x < 0.1, but differ by about 20% at x > 0.2.
the MRST98 parton distributions are: 1. in the DIS scheme; 2. in the MS scheme; 3. at LO; 4. at NLO; 5. with higher twist corrections added.

(1) the MS and DIS parton distributions are not the same; (2) there are significant changes in the gluon distribution when going from LO (MS scheme) to NLO (DIS scheme) and these changes are not well reproduced by a naive LO-to-NLO conversion; and (3) the inclusion of higher twist contributions does not change significantly the parton distributions, but it does affect the value of the strong coupling constant.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a detailed study of the dependence of nucleon partons on the renormalisation scheme and the order in perturbation theory.

the following issues: (i) The determination of the DIS scheme parton distributions, (ii) the effects on the parton distributions of going from LO to the NLO approximation, and (iii) an exploratory study on the effects of possible higher twist terms on the parton distribution functions.

the following topics: (a) the study of the scheme dependence of parton distributions in the DIS scheme and the translation of heavy quark parton distributions in going from MS to DIS; (b) an LO analysis of the parton distributions and comparison with NLO; (c) the inclusion of higher twist effects in the global analysis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NLO analysis is the most reliable one, and that the DIS analysis is the next best one.
the MRST distributions at NLO in the DIS scheme are the best available set of nucleon partons.
the MRST NLO distributions are a good description of the world data, with no need for higher twist contributions, and that the NLO corrections to LO distributions are large and significant.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the NLO distributions in the MS scheme are in good agreement with data, but that the LO results in the DIS scheme, which we take to be our best estimates of the parton densities at LO, are in better agreement with data, especially at low x.
the DIS scheme parton distributions, when compared to the MS ones, are smaller by about 10% in the valence regions, and by 20–30% in the sea regions.
the NLO analysis in the DIS scheme is in excellent agreement with the data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the NLO analysis is in good agreement with DIS scheme results and that the DIS scheme results are in good agreement with experimental data.
the DIS scheme parton distributions are not much different from the MS scheme ones and that the effects of higher twist are small.
, in the context of the MRST parametrizations, the DIS scheme is a better choice than the MS scheme for the description of heavy quark parton distributions.
